title: Examining Kushner’s European Security Framework
gist: CNAS Brussels Sprouts podcast intro: as U.S., Ukrainian and Russian officials hold their first trilateral peace talks in nine months in Abu Dhabi, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner has proposed a pan-European security framework with five goals, while Europeans fear a U.S.-Russia deal made over their heads. Guests Ivo Daalder and Carl Bildt; the page holds only the setup, not the discussion.

themes.theme: Abu Dhabi talks and Kushner framework

insights.claim: American, Ukrainian and Russian officials are meeting in Abu Dhabi for the first trilateral Ukraine peace talks in nine months.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Resumed talks are a catalyst for ceasefire pricing in European defense, energy and Ukraine-reconstruction plays.
insights.quote: the first trilateral peace talks in nine months
insights.locator: This week, American, Ukrainian, and Russian

insights.claim: U.S. Special Envoy Jared Kushner proposed a new European security framework with five goals, including permanent security consultations, crisis communication, greater military transparency and escalation-risk reduction measures.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: A U.S.-Russia-Europe arms-control-style architecture could reshape the European rearmament outlook.
insights.locator: This week, American, Ukrainian, and Russian

insights.claim: Kushner's proposal echoes President Trump's suggestion of a 'big, beautiful agreement' that could include all of Europe, implying negotiations reaching well beyond the war in Ukraine.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Scope creep from Ukraine to continental security raises both upside (de-escalation) and tail risk (concessions on NATO posture).
insights.locator: This week, American, Ukrainian, and Russian

insights.claim: European governments are increasingly concerned Washington could negotiate arrangements with Moscow with far-reaching implications for European security without adequately accounting for European interests.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Fear of a U.S.-Russia bargain sustains European pressure to fund autonomous defense capability.
insights.locator: The proposal comes at a consequential moment

insights.claim: With doubts persisting about the administration's reliability as a security partner, Europe faces growing pressure to define its own approach to negotiating with Russia and the security order it wants.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Structural driver for sustained European defense budgets regardless of a ceasefire.
insights.quote: as doubts persist about this administration’s reliability as a security partner
insights.locator: The proposal comes at a consequential moment
